section: Downloand and install MAXQDA on your device
text:
Downloand and install MAXQDA on your device
If you haven’t yet, download the MAXQDA program to you Mac or Windows computer. Follow the usual procedures for installing software on your device.






If you can’t install MAXQDA on your own device


If you cannot, or do not want to install the MAXQDA software on your compute, you can use the University’s virtual desktop service Illinois AnyWare. This service lets you access a Windows desktop from your own device and use the software installed on that desktop without having to add them to your own device.

title: web
section: Choose the option for the network license
text:
Choose the option for the network license


Open the program. The first time you open MAXQDA on a new device, you will need to set the license information. You should see a screen that says Welcome to MAXQDA and then asks you to choose a license option.
Click on the option that says Connect to your institution's network license





MAXQDA opening screen requesting a license choice

title: web
text:
Enter license information


After you choose to make use of an institutional license, you’ll be prompted to enter the license details.

In the first box asks for your institution’s server address. Enter: maxqda.webstore.illinois.edu
Set the Port to 21990
Make sure the radio button for the last box is checked and enter the license name MAXQDA (all caps included).
Click Connect.





Entering Illinois license information

title: web
section: Key considerations for Teamwork in MAXQDA
text:
Key considerations for Teamwork in MAXQDA

All team members need to be using the same version of MAXQDA for files to import/export or merge correctly.
If you intend to measure inter-coder reliability, you must follow the process as described by MAXQDA for this to work correctly. I highly recommend trying a test version of your process with a sample of your data to ensure that you have the correct procedure in place.1
If you have a team member without current access to MAXQDA, they can still see the data and analysis work by using the free MAXQDA reader program. Using the reader allows a researcher to see how the data has been coded without making any changes to the data or coding.

MAXQDA Manual: Intercoder Agreement

title: web
text:
Exporting to other QDAS programs

The REFI-QDA standard allows some interoperability between qualitative data analysis software programs (such as MAXQDA and Atlas.ti).1
You could use this option if:

You have completed analysis in another program that you no longer have access to.
You have team members at other institutions without access to MAXQDA.
You want to share your data for analysis by other researchers or teams (secondary analysis).


MAXQDA Manual: Export and Import REFI-QDA Projects

title: web
text:
Choose a project location
After you choose to create a new project, you’ll be prompted to choose where you want the project file to be stored.
MAXQDA recommends that you do not open a project file directly form an external storage system like a networked drive, flash drive, or a cloud storage service (like OneDrive, Box, or Google Drive).
If your project and data files are stored in cloud storage, they recommend instead that you make a copy of the file to save directly to your local device. When you have completed your work you can re-upload the project file to the cloud storage.






Managing project files


I recommend that you make a copy of your project each time you work with it and save the new file with a date or other distinguishing feature. This saves previous working copies in case you have problems with the new file or want to return to previous versions of the data.
Example file naming convention: 2026-09-16-Project.mqda.

title: web
section: Where does MAXQDA store project data?
text:
Where does MAXQDA store project data?
You choose where to store your project file and any data you upload to MAXQDA. If you save the project file in a shared folder or cloud service, then the shared settings of those locations will also apply to your data.






Follow data security and privacy requirements for your project


If you are working with high risk, sensitive, or internal data, you must consider your data security requirements when choosing where to store your MAXQDA project data.

title: web
text:
External files


MAXQDA keeps larger data files in a separate folder that allows the data to be accessible for analysis, but without making the project file itself too large. The external file location is the same for all MAXQDA projects, but can be a location you choose.1
Open MAXQDA > Preferences to change the external file settings.

By default, any file over 5MB is saved as an external file. You can change this limit to be larger or smaller.
You can change the location for external files by clicking on the ... button and then choosing a new location on your device.





Open the MAXQDA preferences to set the size for files to be saved external storage and the external file location



MAXQDA Manual: External Files

title: web
section: Text data, including transcripts without time stamps.
text:
Text data, including transcripts without time stamps.
If you have existing transcript files without time stamps or a linked video or audio file, you can upload these to MAXQDA in any of the acceptable text formats.1
To upload text files:

Import > Texts, PDFs, Tables
Select the file(s) you want to upload.
OR drag and drop files from your computer’s file system into the document system window.







Highlights and comments in Word and PDFs will be imported


If you have Word or PDF documents with existing highlighted text or comments, these will be imported to MAXQDA. Highlights are converted to coded segments, with the highlight color becoming a code. Comments will be added to the MAXQDA document as they are in the original document.



MAXQDA Manual: Supported data types

title: web
section: Transcript data: Linking time stamped transcripts with audio or video files
text:
Transcript data: Linking time stamped transcripts with audio or video files
You can also upload transcripts with time stamps and link them with the recording of conversation.1 These transcripts can include the files you get from Zoom or Teams (in the .vtt file format).


To upload and link transcripts and a media file:

Import > Transcripts > Transcripts with Timestampts
Select the file you want to upload
You’ll be prompted to also upload the audio or video file that goes with the transcript. Click OK
Once both files have been uploaded, you will have a text file linked with the media file so you can click on the time stamp to open the recording.





After uploading a transcript with time stamps, you’ll be prompted to upload the corresponding video file.



MAXQDA Manual: Importing Transcripts

title: web
text:
Editing transcripts with time stamps
If you want to edit the transcript after you have uploaded it to MAXQDA, look for the edit/transcribe/view mode toggle in the upper left of the document window.
In edit mode, you can change the text of the transcript.
In transcribe mode, you can edit the location of the time stamps or add new time stamps.

This document is in transcript mode, so time stamps can be edited or added.To add a time stamp,

Navigate to the point in the video or audio file where you want to add the time stamp
Place the cursor in the place in the transcript where you want to add the time stamp
Click enter. This will move the transcript text to a new line and add a time stamp icon that you can use to open the media file at that point.

title: web
text:
Transcribing in MAXQDA
If you do not have transcripts, or draft transcripts, you can use the transcription feature in MAXQDA to create or edit a transcript file.1


To manually transcribe a media file

Import > Audio or Video
Select the video or audio file you want to upload.
Choose Import only from the three options provided. If you choose Link Transcript you’ll be able to upload an existing transcript, while Transcribe opens MAXQDA’s auto transcription tool.2 This is a paid feature not included in the Illinois license.





Options after uploading a video or audio file. Select Import only to allow manual transcription.



MAXQDA Manual: Transcription ModeMAXQDA Manual: Automatic Transcription

title: web
text:
Using transcription mode
In the example below, we’ve uploaded a video file and have transcription mode enabled (#1). Play and pause the video and then type the content in the window (#2). Pressing enter will add a new time stamp.

MAXQDA in transcription mode.

title: web
text:
Survey data
MAXQDA can be used to analyze survey data with open-ended responses, or any data structured in a spreadsheet format.1


Each row in the spreadsheet you upload will become a new document, with the columns created as qualitative data you can code, variables, or both.




Example of a survey response uploaded to MAXQDA. Each question has been created as a coded segment.



MAXQDA Manual: Survey Data from Excel

title: web
text:
Creating codes


The simplest way to create codes is using the New Code icon at the top of the code system. A new window will open where you will enter the name of a code, choose a color for the code, and (optionally) enter a memo.




The new code screen

title: web
text:
Editing codes
Once you’ve created codes, you edit, rearrange, and merge them as needed.


Most options for managing codes can be accessed by right-clicking on a code. You’ll see a list of code options.




Right click on a code to see a full menu of options, including re-naming or changing the color

title: web
text:
Organizing codes
Codes can be organized in a hierarchical system as you create them, or can be organized later. Your code system can be as complex as you need, with as many levels of hierarchy as makes sense for your project.
To add a new sub-code: hover over the code and look for the green plus icon.
To make a code a sub-code of another, drag the sub-code on top of the parent code.

title: web
text:
Applying codes to text data


When you select a segment of the data and right click, you’ll see several options for coding:

With a new code. If you select this option, you’ll be prompted to create the new code.
In Vivo: This option will label the data with the text of the segment, creating a new code if one does not already exist.
With a recent code: There are three recently applied codes listed here that could be applied.

Alternately, if the code you want to apply already exists, you can select the segment and then click the code in the code system window.




The options for coding that display when you select a data segment and right click.

title: web
section: Changing document display to see codes
text:
Changing document display to see codes


MAXQDA does not show the data you’ve coded in the code color by default. Instead you’ll need to enable the display of coded segments:

Look for the ... in the upper left corner of the document window and click this icon to show the display options. This menu has several options for how the codes are displayed with your data.
Check the Coded segments in code color box to show the data in the color assigned to the code.





Document display options. Check the Coded segments in code color option to highlight data in the color assigned to the code.

title: Jess Hagman
text: Hi, I’m Jess Hagman, a librarian at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. I use this website to share workshop materials and presentations I’ve offered.

title: Jess Hagman
text: Recent workshops

title: web
section: Types of research findings or outcomes
text:
Types of research findings or outcomes

Frequencies or counts
Topical surveys
Thematic
Theories or explanations
Ethnographic description

title: web
text:
Describing your methods and values

Qualitative is a big category, with lots of different types of data, analysis strategies, and ideas about what “quality” looks like. (Small & Calarco, 2022). Under this “Big Tent” (Tracy, 2025) of qualitative research, it can be hard for new researchers to find their place and what makes their research credible to readers. (Roulston & Bhattacharya, 2018)
When readers have different ideas about what makes research high quality, you may receive feedback or evaluation that is based on different assumptions about rigor. (Clarke et al., 2025; Moura et al., 2025).
To counter this challenge, your paper should explain how you analyzed the data and what you believe makes the analysis credible. (Smagorinsky, 2008; Staller & Krumer-Nevo, 2013)

title: web
section: Sorting data into groups or variables
text:
Sorting data into groups or variables
The concept of variables is used more frequently in quantitative research, but we can use this language to think of groups within the data that we want to use for comparison in order to answer our research questions.1
Variables can be:

pre-existing: such as types of data, groups of participants, research sites, or phases of data collection
or, identified as you analyze and applied to the data for comparisons, such as when you identify a group of participants who have an experience relevant to your research questions.


❓ What existing groups or variables are there in your data?

I use variables here because this is the term used in MAXQDA, the QDA software available on campus.

title: web
section: Transcribing data from media to text formats
text:
Transcribing data from media to text formats








The practice of transforming audio or video content into text for the purposes of analysis.
Potential tools:

Meeting software transcripts (e.g. Zoom, Teams)
Transcription software (Trint, Otter)
Manual transcription support - provides tools to facilitate typing what you hear (e.g. MAXQDA, oTranscribe)
Illinois Mediaspace - create and edit a transcription of uploaded media.

title: web
text:
Coding




Labeling segments of the data with a topic, concept, or other descriptor. These codes allow us to look up from the specifics of individuals or cases and look across the data to identify patterns. (Richards, 2021)
While coding is used in many qualitative methods, it is not a required element of every qualitative project. (Coffey, 1996; Saldaña, 2025).
Coding can be done using analog versions of your data, with ordinary productivity software, or software developed specifically for qualitative data analysis (sometimes called CAQDAS or QDAS).

title: web
text:
Analyzing coded data
Once you have coded your data, you can use the coded data set to ask further questions about the data and move towards research findings.

title: web
text:
Writing
Across qualitative texts, you’ll find a frequent recommendation to write throughout the process of collecting and analyzing data.
Writing has you work has several benefits, including:

Writing as thinking: Sometimes writing out an explanation serves as a way of thinking through a challenge or question in a way that just internal pondering cannot.(Keane, 2022; Montgomery & Bailey, 2007)
Writing as documentation: Have a record of how you analyzed the data and how your interpretation developed will help you write about that process and communicate the quality of your analysis.(Kalpokas & Radivojevic, 2022)
Writing as kindness to your future self: The version of yourself who writes the paper or dissertation that comes out of this analysis will appreciate having as much previously written information as possible. You may be able to edit and use your memos or other writing in your final product.

title: Creating a new project in MAXQDA
text:
When you first open MAXQDA, you’ll be prompted tho choose what project file you want to work with.
The three options are to:

Create an entirely new project.
Open an existing MAXQDA project.
Create a file that contains example data for exploring MAXQDA features.









The opening screen of MAXQDA where you can (1) create a new project (2) open an existing project or (3) open a file with example data.




Figure 1








After you choose to create a new project, you’ll be prompted to choose where you want the project file to be stored.


You choose where to store your project file and any data you upload to MAXQDA. If you save the project file in a shared folder or cloud service, then the shared settings of those locations will also apply to your data.
You should choose a storage location that meets any data security and confidentiality protections required by the IRB application or project design.






WarningSaving to external or cloud storage?



MAXQDA recommends that you do not open a project file directly form an external storage system like a networked drive, flash drive, or a cloud storage service (like OneDrive, Box, or Google Drive).
If your project and data files are stored in cloud storage, they recommend instead that you make a copy of the file to save directly to your local device. When you have completed your work you can re-upload the project file to the cloud storage.





MAXQDA keeps larger data files in a separate folder that allows the data to be accessible for analysis, but without making the project file itself too large. The external file location is the same for all MAXQDA projects, but can be a location you choose.



Open MAXQDA > Preferences to change the external file settings.

By default, any file over 5MB is saved as an external file. You can change this limit to be larger or smaller.
You can change the location for external files by clicking on the ... button and then choosing a new location on your device.









Open the MAXQDA preferences to set the size for files to be saved external storage and the external file location




Figure 2
